title: How do we measure and name these four angles?
description: Four angles at the point T are read on a protractor, and each reading is compared with ninety and one hundred eighty degrees to give its name. The last angle has the same arms as the third but goes the long way round, so it is the rest of the full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the measure on the protractor, then compare it with ninety and one hundred eighty to name the kind; the long way round is the full turn take away the short way. Watch for students who give the same measure to both angles with the same arms.

video_script.why: The child reads each angle on a protractor, names it by comparing with ninety and one hundred eighty degrees, and finds the long way round angle from the full turn.
video_script.substitution: Read 30, 60 and 102 degrees from the protractor, name each by comparing with 90 and 180, and take 102 away from 360 for the angle the long way round.
video_script.anchor: the book's figure: a protractor at the vertex T with the points P, R, Q and W on its arms
video_script.payoff_line: The reading gives the measure, and the measure gives the name

final_answer.spoken: the angle P T R is thirty degrees and acute, P T Q is sixty degrees and acute, P T W is one hundred two degrees and obtuse, and W T P is two hundred fifty eight degrees and reflex

maths_rules: ∠WTP is the same arms the long way round: 360° − 102° = 258°
video_script.design: One protractor at T with the arm T P on the zero line. The readings are shown as arcs; the long way round arc is drawn in rose on the outside.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a protractor with its centre on the point T; four angles marked by arcs: P T R, P T Q, P T W and W T P

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about measuring angles.
<bookmark mark='fig'/>A protractor sits on the point T.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four angles are marked, P T R, P T Q, P T W and W T P.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What does each one measure, and what is its name?

beats.on_screen: the figure holds still on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the protractor with its centre on T and its zero line along T P; a tick marks where an arm crosses the scale; the marks 90° and 180° are lit on the scale

marks.centre: the centre of the protractor sits on T
marks.zero: the zero line lies along the arm T P
marks.read: a tick marks where another arm crosses the scale
marks.marks: the marks 90° and 180° light up on the scale

narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>A protractor measures an angle in degrees.
Its centre sits on the vertex.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Its zero line lies along one arm.
<bookmark mark='read'/>We read the scale where the other arm crosses it.
<bookmark mark='marks'/>Then ninety and one hundred eighty tell us the name.

beats.on_screen: Given: angles PTR, PTQ, PTW and WTP at the point T

marks.given: the four angle names are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four angles at the point T.

beats.on_screen: To find: the measure and the kind of each angle

marks.find: the words measure and kind are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the measure and the kind of each angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: ∠PTR = 30° and ∠PTQ = 60°, both less than 90°, so both are acute

marks.first: the arm T R crosses the scale at 30° and the arm T Q at 60°
marks.name: both readings are placed before the 90° mark and labelled acute

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, read the scale at the arms T R and T Q.
They read thirty and sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Both are less than ninety, so both angles are acute.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: ∠PTW = 102°, which is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse

marks.second: the arm T W crosses the scale at 102°
marks.name: 102° is placed between the 90° and 180° marks and labelled obtuse

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, read the scale at the arm T W.
It reads one hundred two degrees.
<bookmark mark='name'/>That is more than ninety and less than one hundred eighty, so the angle is obtuse.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: ∠WTP is the same arms the long way round, so ∠WTP = 360° − 102°

marks.round: the arc for W T P is drawn on the outside, the long way round, in rose
marks.take: 102° is taken away from the full turn 360°

narration: <bookmark mark='round'/>Step three, the angle W T P has the same arms but goes the long way round.
<bookmark mark='take'/>It is the rest of the full turn, so take away one hundred two from three hundred sixty.

marks.check: the two angles at T are added and fill the full circle
marks.name: the long way round angle is placed past the 180° mark and labelled reflex

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question.
The angles P T W and W T P must fill a full turn together.
<bookmark mark='name'/>The long way round is past one hundred eighty, so that angle is reflex.

marks.pay: the words reading, measure and name glow in order

beats.colours: acute = teal, obtuse = amber, long way round = rose
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The reading gives the measure, and the measure gives the name.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The angle P T R is thirty degrees and acute.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The angle P T Q is sixty degrees and acute.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The angle P T W is one hundred two degrees and obtuse.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The angle W T P is two hundred fifty eight degrees and reflex.
